title: Dedicated Capacity: Audit, Traceability & Revenue Recognition SOP
author: Marcos Liang
content:
Summary:
This Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) defines the end-to-end controls, artifacts, and operational steps required to: (1) ensure procurement and contract records for Dedicated capacity are auditable and traceable; (2) align forecasting and recognition handoffs between Sales, Procurement, Finance, and Engineering; and (3) establish deterministic billing triggers and revrec (revenue recognition) treatment for multi-month or multi-year capacity commitments.

Purpose and scope:
- Purpose: Reduce revenue leakage and close the observability gap between signed commitments and invoices for Dedicated GPU capacity contracts.
- Scope: Applies to all Dedicated capacity contracts, addenda, renewals, and related purchase orders (POs) executed from 2024-01-01 onward. Excluded: ad-hoc hosted API usage, marketplace reseller transactions (see related pages).

Key definitions:
- Dedicated Capacity Commitment: A contractual reservation of compute capacity (measured in dGPU-hours, slots, or nodes) for a defined period with billing and revrec terms.
- Billing Trigger: The event or milestone that converts a contractual commitment into an invoiceable event (examples: contract effective date, delivery acceptance sign-off, first-day-of-service).
- Usage Reconciliation: Daily/weekly process comparing provisioned capacity vs. customer-reported usage to validate billable amounts and credits.

Roles & ownership:
- Finance (RevRec Owner): Primary owner for interpretation of accounting treatment, revenue schedule, and audits. Responsible: Ana Torres.
- Legal: Contract clause validation, signature evidence, and risk acceptance. Responsible: Priya Menon.
- Sales / Account Executive: Capture signed commercial terms and ensure contract metadata completeness in CRM. Responsible: assigned AE on each deal.
- Procurement / Ops: Ensure POs and vendor-side paperwork are linked to contracts and that procurement approvals are in Concur/SAP. Responsible: Procurement Ops team.
- Engineering (Platform Owner): Validate provisioning events, capacity tagging, and serve as source-of-truth for actual capacity allocation. Responsible: SRE/Platform oncall.
- Billing / Platform Billing: Generate invoice artifacts and post invoices to Stripe/ERP. Responsible: Billing team.

Required artifacts & metadata (minimum):
- Signed contract PDF (e-sign evidence), stored in Contract Repository with contract_id.
- Commercial term summary (one-pager) containing: customer_id, contract_id, commitment_units, unit_definition (dGPU-hour/node), start_date, end_date, billing_trigger, billing_frequency, cancellation_terms, renewal_terms, pricing tiers, discounts, and approved revenue treatment (deferred / recognized).
- PO or purchase authorization with PO_number linked to contract_id.
- Provisioning confirmation (engineering event) indicating capacity allocated: provision_event_id, timestamp, capacity_tag, region, and tenant_id.
- Acceptance sign-off (if required): signed acceptance PDF or account_owner email thread linked in repository.

End-to-end workflow (step-by-step):
1) Deal capture and CRM hygiene
   1.1 AE enters commercial terms into CRM Opportunity using the Dedicated Capacity template. Required fields: contract_id (pre-allocated), commitment_units, billing_trigger, and revenue_profile_code.
   1.2 AE requests Legal to draft contract and lists required artifacts (PO, KMS/HSM requirements if private deployment, compliance addenda).
2) Contract execution & ingestion
   2.1 Legal executes contract. Legal uploads signed PDF to Contract Repository and tags with contract_id.
   2.2 Legal sets contract_status = "executed" and notifies Finance and Procurement via #contracts-signed channel.
3) Procurement PO and payment terms
   3.1 Procurement confirms PO raised and records PO_number in Contract Repository.
   3.2 Procurement verifies billing milestones align with billing_trigger.
4) Provisioning and acceptance
   4.1 Engineering provisions capacity and emits provision_event to the Capacity Registry (Kafka topic: capacity.provisioned). Event must include contract_id and capacity_tag.
   4.2 If acceptance required, Account Owner completes Acceptance Form; acceptance_event is logged to Contract Repository.
5) Billing trigger evaluation & invoice generation
   5.1 Billing system subscribes to provisioned and acceptance events and evaluates billing_trigger for each contract_id.
   5.2 Billing generates invoice, attaches contract_id, PO_number, provision_event_id, and posts invoice to ERP.
6) RevRec & journal entries
   6.1 Finance receives invoice and contract metadata, verifies revenue_profile_code and posts appropriate journal entries (deferred revenue vs. immediate recognition) per ASC 606 policy.
   6.2 Monthly: RevRec team runs a reconciliation report between Contract Repository and General Ledger.
7) Usage reconciliation & credits
   7.1 Weekly reconciliation compares actual consumed capacity (platform metrics) vs. committed capacity. Variances greater than the tolerance threshold (see thresholds table) trigger credit review.

Thresholds & acceptance criteria (table):
- Billing Tolerance Thresholds:
  - Initial provisioning delay: 72 hours (engineering must provision within 72 hours of effective_date)
  - Capacity variance tolerance: 5% (if usage < committed - 5% sustained for >30 days, investigate for credit/reschedule)
  - Documentation completeness: 100% required fields present before invoice generation

Audit trail checklist (must be present for external audit):
- Signed contract with embedded signature metadata (signature id, signer email, timestamp).
- Contract Repository entry linking contract_id -> CRM opportunity id -> provision_event_id -> invoice_id.
- PO with payment terms or ack.
- Provisioning log retained for 7 years.
- Notification history (#contracts-signed slack thread or equivalent).

Sample contract metadata JSON (for ingestion pipeline):
{
  "contract_id": "RC-2026-0457",
  "customer_id": "CUST-1998",
  "commitment_units": "4000-dgpu-hours",
  "unit_definition": "dGPU-hour (A100)",
  "start_date": "2026-04-01",
  "end_date": "2027-03-31",
  "billing_trigger": "provisioned",
  "billing_frequency": "monthly",
  "po_number": "PO-8821",
  "revenue_profile_code": "DED-ANNUAL-DEF"
}

Operational playbook: exception handling & corrections:
- Missing PO at invoice time: Billing holds invoice and notifies Procurement; 48-hour SLA to supply PO. If overdue, tag invoice_status = "on-hold-pending-po" and escalate to Director of Procurement.
- Provisioned without contract_id: Engineering flags event, quarantines capacity, and notifies Sales and Legal. Capacity remains non-billable until contract_id reconciled.
- Overbilling discovered: Create remediation ticket, credit customer, and adjust deferred revenue schedule; Finance to log a correction memo and obtain VP-Finance approval for adjustments > $50k.

Forecasting & handoff rules (aligning Sales -> Finance):
- Sales must submit a Forecast Intake within 48 hours of contract execution including ARR-equivalent and committed capacity start_date.
- Finance updates the capacity commitment pool and annotates forecast model with a probability = 100% once contract_status = executed and PO received.
- For negotiated phased starts (staggered provisioning), Sales must provide provisioning_schedule with dates and expected unit allocations.

Monitoring & KPIs (owned by Finance Ops):
- DSO impact from Dedicated deals (days-from-effective-to-invoice) target: <= 10 days.
- Forecast drift (committed vs. billed) target: <= 3% monthly.
- Audit completeness score (artifact coverage per contract) target: 100% at invoice time.

Escalation matrix:
- Day 0-2: AE & Procurement Ops
- Day 3-7: Sales Leader + Procurement Manager
- Day 8+: VP Sales + VP Finance + Legal (for contract remediation)

Appendix A — sample journal entry mapping:
- Invoice for pre-paid annual capacity (billing at start): Debit: Accounts Receivable; Credit: Deferred Revenue. Monthly recognition: Debit Deferred Revenue; Credit: Revenue (per capacity consumption schedule).

Appendix B — quick checklist for Sales at contract close:
- [ ] Contract uploaded and tagged with contract_id
- [ ] PO is created and linked (if required)
- [ ] Provisioning schedule (or start date) provided to Platform
- [ ] Revenue profile code selected and signed off by Finance
- [ ] Acceptance criteria documented (if applicable)

Document maintenance and owners:
- Document owner: Ana Torres (Finance, RevRec)
- Process owner: Priya Menon (Legal)
- Review cadence: Quarterly or after any accounting policy change.
